contexts.text: The mind then determines its view outside of itself to doctrinal things.
Evident from the view of the Things in the internal sense.
He has the habit (of always) regarding himself. Described.
He filled the whole surrounding sphere, which was one of self-regard.
Hence the mental view, apperception, and utterance of each thing is more prompt.
He could view my thoughts and affections inwardly.
When I was reading some of the Psalms, the interior view or mind of the Spirits was opened.
A representation of the Lord's Kingdom in a universal mental view. Signified, Explained.
A representation of goods and truths in a mental view of the constellations, Signified, Explained.
The Lord's insight into the cause from His interior man. Treated of.
It is the interior sight or view which perceives...
A view from what is higher into what is lower, or from what is interior into what is exterior, is called influx. Explained.
Thus they have regard to themselves, and not to others...
So far as (this merely human rational truth) views the things above itself... it does not acknowledge them.
They are perceived in one view of the thought.
Still, the Angels have... a very perfect mental view of future things.
So that the mental view of all things which are of doctrine is from the Rational.
Regarded in itself, prayer is a speaking to God, and some internal view then of the things concerned in the prayer.
A mental looking at the cause. Signified, Explained.
The Lord's looking at this state of the human race...
The Lord's insight from the Divine Spiritual. Signified.
To understand is the same as to view from the sight of the mind.
That man can look from within into the things in himself which are beneath, is known...
Thought and insight from the Divine. Signified.
To see, because predicated of the Lord, = to view from the Divine.
The Lord's thought and insight from the Divine. Signified.
Such desire that the things of faith should be believed simply, without any view (or insight) from the Rational.
For a man receives only so much from others as... he acquires by a mental view of the matter in himself.
(External and internal truth) cannot be conjoined together until self-regard begins to cease, and a regarding of the neighbour begins to be felt.
(These words) involve a mental view and the derivative excited affection.
The interior viewings and perceptions of Things belong to the understanding.
If they look to the Infinite...
Otherwise it would be to look into thick darkness.
Evident from the view of the Things in the internal sense.
At the first sight this appears remote.
He loves to look into, and does look into, things still more intricate.
These (truths) cannot come to his mental view and apprehension until goods acts as the chief.
Those who, by the Knowledges of good and truth, have acquired for themselves the faculty of viewing Things from what is general. Described.
Interior truths (are those which) are more closely under the view of the Rational.
(These) cause truth and good to be perceived by a mental view almost unlimited.
At the first mental view of these things, they reject them...
They who have a... more interior insight, see confirmations.
In this way they destroy in themselves, the insight from what is higher or more interior.

They who are in faith separated... have no interior insight; for they who are not in the affection of charity are in external sight only; that is, in a lower mental view (or insight), from which no one can possibly see higher things.
Hence no one (now) knows from mental view, thus not from perception, whether truth be really truth; but only from doctrine.
(Such) cannot elevate the mind's view... except from self.
For it is good into which the Lord inflows, and gives intelligence and wisdom, and consequently a higher insight, and also a perception as to whether it is so, or is not so.
(These things) effect a higher insight with the spiritual man, by which he can see, and also perceive, whether a thing is true or not.
He turns the attention of all to himself...
It was not the Sensuous things themselves that were rejected... but the mental views, or thoughts, from them.
In speech, the directing of the attention to person narrows... the idea.
What a man thinks about is directly under his view...
In proportion as (thought and speech) are determined... abstractedly to Things... the insight becomes higher, and consequently more universal.
Man is man from this... that when he thinks what is true and wills what is good, he can contemplate the Divine, and receive it perceptibly.
Truths... remain as scientifics until the man begins to consider (or view) them with his own sight...
The more there are who direct their mental look into one Subject, the stronger is his power... His force is augmented in proportion to the plurality of the concordant mental looks.
For the things which are directly under the mental view are in the middle... (Compare AC 6084.)
The internal sight is determined to those things which afford the greatest delight... and it fixes a direct view upon them...
For scientifics fall under the spiritual view.
At last there comes into existence from the internal a mental view of these (truths), that is, reason and understanding.

The Intellectual in man... consists in the mental view of Things from such things as are of experience and knowledge; and also in the mental view of causes from effects, and of things consequent from the connection of the causes.
The Lord is, in Heaven, the Centre of the mental regards of all.
They are in a pre-eminent faculty of understanding and perceiving, according to the degree of their insight from what is interior.

For he feared to look upon God () = lest they should be injured by the presence of the Divine Itself... To look upon God = the presence of the Divine Itself, because the Lord is presented as present before man... by an internal looking, which is effected by means of the faith which is from charity.
They who are in the light of Heaven, ... before confirmation, apperceive, by a mental view looking at the scientifics which are beneath... whether a truth is to be confirmed or not.
But not, as before, in the midst directly under the mind's view.
They had intently viewed the bird's changes.
In order that whenever they looked at anything, they might remember it.
(The celestial Angels) are under the Lord's immediate view.
At the first view and apperception (of truth Divine such as it is in Heaven) man would reject it.
Afterwards, the Things laid up in the external memory are subjected to the sight or view of the internal man...
Lest (memory truth) be extinguished under his mental view. Signified, Explained.

Under his hand = under his mental view; for the hand = the power which belongs to spiritual truth, thus which belongs to mental view; for mental view is effected from this truth, and is apperception; for the truths of the literal sense... stored up in the natural memory, form there as it were a field for the mental view of the internal man...
When such are in the mental view of what is just and good...
Such do not see what is just and good, because they are in regard for self and gain.
For falsities... form the natural mind itself and its insight as to the things of the Church and Heaven.
They keep their mental view fixed on themselves and the world.
Some of the learned, by a looking into their own thoughts... have observed...
This general idea... is annihilated when it is placed under the view in the midst...
For the things which man views intensely in thought are presented before him.
The view (of the celestial Angels) does not stop at such things as are before their eyes; but they see the interior things... to which they correspond...
(Such) cannot be elevated into the light of Heaven, and view the Things of the Church which are beyond its doctrinal things.
True intelligence and wisdom consist in seeing and perceiving what is true and good, and thence what is false and evil... from interior insight and perception.
Their erudition does not rise beyond such things as appear in the world... which they keep in the memory, and view almost materially.
They regard the things of the Word just as others do matters of mere memory knowledge, and do not make them Things for thought, nor for any insight of an enlightened rational mind.
Man takes with him all the natural memory; but the things in it are not under his view... as while he lived (here).
For the interior mind of man looks into the Things of the natural memory...
If the life of man is regarded and examined by means of rational insight, it is found to be threefold...
Everyone can see, from some rational insight, that...
If you collect together all things you know, and submit them to the insight of your mind...
Who that is able to observe the essence of love, cannot see this?
At first sight these appear distinct...
If the Lord were among the Angels in Heaven, He could not have the universe under His view... DLW 106.
For all things are under the Sun's view...
7. (This) is evident to everyone who is willing to survey this from rational insight.
(The thought of the spirit) views the things which are of thought from the memory as beneath itself.
For whatever is in the midst is directly under the view, and is seen and perceived.
Fix your look on the paper. They did so. (The result.)
When I fixed my view on that light, it receded to the sides...
(This) may be concluded and seen from insight and examination alone.
(The wives said), There is scarcely a time in the day in which our penetrative thought quite recedes from our husbands, or is absent from them. CL 294:2.
Some were favouring and looking at me...
If we regard works thus...
How can anyone shun evils... without some self-inspection?
A judge... collects the evidence into one view in the higher region of his mind.
Like a looking to the sign of Satan...
All these things are perceived by a Spirit by spiritual insight alone, without description.
By a general view...
The mental regards of Spirits.
That the Lord can enable anyone, by a spiritual idea, to view interior Things.
If the Angels merely look at... an evil Spirit, he is tortured... SE 2519.
With a continual looking to their own advantage.
Others are tormented with envy from a mere view of the happiness of the Angels.
What a look may effect in the other life, thus what a look of trust and faith in the Lord, can be known only to one who lives there. SE 3002, Explained. SE 3003.
That a mental view of ends... distinguishes man from the brutes. Explained.
That Spirits are found and affected by means of my lookings. Explained.
And on the other hand, by their looks at me, Spirits take [things] out of my memory: this is a general look...
This is a magical looking at [a person]. Explained.
A looking by faith can effect all things. Explained... But faith is such that in proportion as the looking to the Lord is from man... it has no efficacy.
This speech is... intuitive of (that is, it looks at) the other's thought...
This is not perceptible to them on account of the regardings of particulars.
It was merely the Society and its looking at [him] which caused his thought.
When I fixed my look on a fly, the evil Spirit could speak only about the fly.
Whatever was in the idea about the persons, he collected, and kept the attention (or look) therein.
They suppose faith to be only a kind of looking to the Lord.
When looking at (those Spirits) was granted...
With a sole regard to wealth.

When the looks and ideas of many Spirits were [fixed] upon her who was a Subject, her forces of thinking were increased; for in proportion to the number of looks [directed] at one, in the same proportion she acts more strongly. I had observed that she had magically attracted the looks of others, by accepting the things which inflowed, and thus proceeding to those from whom the influx came.
When I determined my look... upon their feet... their genitals were indrawn.
A sphere as of a mere looking, without anything determinate...
They regard faith as a mere view, or thought.
Faith without good works is... merely intellectual faith...
I answered by a like intuitive speech. (See Speak.)
He who looks at generals from particulars goes astray in every object of his contemplation.
Shown by a looking into the eye...
Charles XII saw every single thing around him with one look.
I looked at others with an intent gaze, and they were affected by my look...
At this day, man does not believe in heavenly things... when they are under his view, in the midst. Explained.
Truths, with them, had been scientifics without any sight [of them].
(The English) have... an interior sight, which is a sight that is receptive of intuition.
Without such a view [of me] they would not have known me.
By lookings at various parts of the head, they explore...
(Such) have no extended mental view. DMin 4745.
The interior sight (of the English) is called an intuitive, receptive, and affirmative, and also a confirmative, sight.
When the view of reputation and gain is taken away...
They are always looking at themselves.
The show bread.
The thought of their spirit is fixed in the consideration of self.
(This) can be seen from common intuition.
The other limit is the seeing and thinking [faculty].
All things which are in the natural mind from the spiritual mind come under the view, and into the perception, of the man.
Faith is acknowledgement, and a view from acknowledgement.
The interiors of the mind are (then) kept by the Lord in a looking to Himself.
A man who is in genuine truths from the sense of the letter... can disperse the whole diabolical crew... by a mere look and an effort of will.
No one can speak to another there unless he looks directly at him.
